newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says underperforming assets to be sold.
newsitem.headline: BHP says underperforming assets to be sold.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday that any assets that did not in future return at least 10 percent on the cost of capital would be considered for sale.

"The returns being achieved currently are not acceptable," BHP's general manager, finance, Graeme McGregor said at the company's annual briefing following the release of its profit result last Friday.
BHP announced a 1996/97 (June/May) net profit of A$410 million, 60.8 percent lower than the year-ago level.

The result included abnormal writedowns of A$976 million, with more than half from the copper division led by Magma in the United States. There were writedowns in the other three divisions -- steel petroleum, and minerals.
"The first priority is to concentrate on those assets that have return of capital of less than eight percent," McGregor said at the briefing.

"That (the priority is..) in a year's time no established business or integrated business chain where more than one asset group is involved will be earning less than 10 percent return on capital or action will be taken to lift returns or the asset will be sold," he said.
